subject: Budget & procurement cadence — monthly token range and PO timing
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <samira@atlashealth.com>, Liam O'Neil <liam.oneil@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Budget & procurement cadence — monthly token range and PO timing

Hi Samira / Liam —

Thanks again for the time this morning — appreciated the walkthrough of your inference flows and the cost sensitivity on the patient-search embeddings. Quick recap + two asks so we can line up an appropriate quote and procurement plan: 

1) Volume profile (what I heard)
   - Search embedding-heavy tests: ~50% of tokens (short sequences)
   - Multi-turn summaries / triage: longer-sequence generation (about 30% of tokens)
   - Background analytics / batch reranks: remaining 20%

2) Banding ask — please confirm which of the monthly bands below is closest to your likely steady state next quarter (we can model spikes separately):
   - Band alpha: 100–150M tokens/mo
   - Band beta: 150–300M tokens/mo
   - Band gamma: 300–450M tokens/mo

3) Procurement note I heard: any vendor spend > $50k/year triggers legal & procurement onboarding; PO lead times are ~4–6 weeks once vendor setup is complete. If that’s changed, flag it.

Attached is the pricing breakout (redwood-pricing-1M-token-breakdown-v2.xlsx) — it shows per-1M-token unit economics across on-demand vs committed tiers. I sketched provisional $/1M targets in the sheet; happy to walk through numbers in a quick call.

Next steps (please):
 - Confirm preferred band (alpha/beta/gamma) and if you need separate pilot vs production bands.
 - Confirm procurement threshold (annual $ trigger) and whether PO cadence will be monthly or quarterly for initial rollout.
 - If helpful, can schedule a 30-minute procurement sync with our finance ops next week.

Thanks — I’ll get Marissa to draft a starting quote once you confirm the band.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
viv ek@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0132

From: Samira Patel <samira@atlashealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Neil <liam.oneil@atlashealth.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Aug 2027 11:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Budget & procurement cadence — monthly token range and PO timing

Thanks, Vivek — great session. Quick answers and a couple clarifications below.

- Volume: based on the pilot and internal forecasts we expect: 100–350M tokens/month depending on adoption speed. The most-likely path is starting around 120–160M/mo (pilot -> month 1), then ramping toward the 250–350M range by Q4 if the clinician feedback looks good.

- Unit economics target: the team is aiming for a blended target of $80–$120 / 1M tokens for long-term budgeting. Lower is obviously better — but that range would be workable for product economics.

- Procurement thresholds: our procurement policy requires vendor setup + legal review for any agreement > $50k/year. PO processing (once vendor is set up) is typically 2–3 weeks; the vendor setup itself can take 4–6 weeks unless expedited. For initial pilots we'll likely do month-to-month POs under $10k for the first code freeze, then move to quarterly or annual as we commit.

Attached: atlas-procurement-req.pdf — procurement contact info + vendor onboarding checklist.

If you can sketch 2–3 pricing scenarios that map to our bands (pilot, conservative ramp, full adoption) that would help the internal conversations. Also: is there a committed / reserved option that meaningfully lowers the $/1M token price if we sign to a 12-month commit?

Appreciate it — Samira
Director of Product, Atlas Health
samira@atlashealth.com | +1 212 555 0899

Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Budget & procurement cadence — monthly token range and PO timing

Samira — thanks for the clarity. Below are three sketched scenarios that map bands to target $/1M and estimated monthly spend. These are conservative on compute + include expected prefix/caching benefits; final quote will show line items for embeddings vs generation tokens.

Scenario A — Pilot / conservative
- Band alpha (100–150M tokens/mo)
 - Proposed unit price: $130 / 1M tokens (on-demand style pilot rate)
 - Estimated monthly spend: $13,000 — $19,500

Scenario B — Ramp to steady state
- Band beta (150–300M tokens/mo)
 - Proposed unit price: $110 / 1M tokens (3–6 month commitment suggested)
 - Estimated monthly spend: $16,500 — $33,000

Scenario C — High-adoption / committed
- Band gamma (300–450M tokens/mo)
 - Proposed unit price: $95 / 1M tokens (12-mo reserved commit available)
 - Estimated monthly spend: $28,500 — $42,750

Notes / trade-offs:
 - Committed 12-month reserved capacity reduces unit price (example above for Scenario C). We can model stepped discounts based on committed TPUs / target RUs.
 - We can also do a hybrid: a small monthly on-demand pilot + reserved capacity for critical steady workloads to reduce risk.
 - If procurement needs to keep spend < $50k/year early, Scenario A keeps you well below that threshold; Scenario B starts to approach procurement trigger if you move to yearly commitment.

Next actions I propose:
 - You confirm which scenario you want us to model for a formal quote (A/B/C).
 - If Scenario B or C, confirm whether you can sign a 12-month commitment (we'll show committed pricing vs month-to-month).
 - Schedule a 30-minute procurement sync — I suggest Tue/Thu next week; Marissa will draft the quote and Aditya can include a tech appendix on caching and expected token reduction.

I’ve attached an updated pricing sheet and a short preliminary SOW link in HubSpot (see related links). If this looks reasonable I’ll ask Marissa to produce an official quote and get finance involved for vendor setup lead time estimates.

Best,
Vivek
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
